explanation: The bucket must be looked up before it can be scanned. The scan checks each existing entry's key; when it finds a match, it overwrites that slot and returns immediately — that return is what prevents the update path from also falling through to the append/size-increment lines below. Only when the loop finishes without finding a match (the key is genuinely new) does execution reach bucket.append and table.size += 1, which must run together and in that order so an update never inflates size.
prompt: Drag these statements into the order that makes put() update an existing key in place, or append and grow the table when the key is new — never both.
